programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: What happens when a literary novelist tries to write popular romantic fiction? To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks. Help is at hand from the publishers themselves, a prolific Mills and Boon author and some avid romance fans, as Duffy's quest to create the perfect romantic novel takes her from London to Italy on a journey that is both an insight into the art of romantic fiction and the joy and frustration of writing itself.

programme.title: Girls in Bands at the BBC
programme.desc: Compilation celebrating some guitar band performances at the BBC that feature some of the best female musicians in rock. Beginning with the oft-forgotten American group Fanny performing You're the One, it's a journey along rock's spectrum from the 1970s to now. The selection includes the powerful vocals of Elkie Brooks on Vinegar Joe's Proud to Be a Honky Woman, the mesmerising poetry of Patti Smith's Horses and the upbeat energy of The Go-Go's on We Got the Beat. Mighty basslines come courtesy of Tina Weymouth on Psycho Killer and Kim Gordon on Sugar Kane, whilst we trace the line of indie rock from the Au Pairs through Lush, Elastica and Garbage to current band Savages.

programme.title: Wild
programme.desc: Documentary presenting an intimate portrait of one of Britain's most charming wild animals, following a family of water voles living on a canal in Derbyshire though a typical year. The picturesque Cromford canal used to serve the region's cotton mills. Now, having been deserted, it serves as a perfect water vole paradise. For these hyperactive little mammals, a year is nearly a lifetime. They spend their lives in a frenzy of activity - swimming, feeding and breeding - the latter of most necessity, since water voles are becoming a rarity.

programme.title: Full Circle with Michael Palin
programme.desc: Michael Palin circles the Pacific Rim through 18 countries. After a journey on a rusty ferry through the dangerous Sulu Sea, he arrives in Borneo at monsoon time. Across the equator in Java, the most densely populated island in the world, he visits the largest monument in the southern hemisphere.

programme.title: Ran
programme.desc: Akira Kurosawa's epic masterpiece is a reworking of Shakespeare's King Lear set in medieval Japan. After a lifetime of battles, 70-year-old Lord Hidetora announces that he is passing his authority to his eldest son Taro. The youngest son Saburo protests and is banished from the kingdom. But instead of fulfilling their father's wishes, Taro and middle brother Jiro are disloyal to the former lord and attack his castle. Hidetora survives but following his sons' betrayal is now losing his mind. When Jiro has his brother murdered, the banished Saburo and his allies return to fight a battle against the remaining brother. In Japanese with English subtitles.

programme.title: The Medici: Makers of Modern Art
programme.desc: Documentary in which Andrew Graham-Dixon reveals how the Medici family transformed Florence through sculpture, painting and architecture, and created a world where masterpieces fetch millions today. Without the money and patronage of the Medici we might never have heard of artists such as Donatello, Michelangelo or Botticelli. Graham-Dixon examines how a family of shadowy, corrupt businessmen, driven by greed and ambition, became the financial engine behind the Italian Renaissance.

programme.desc: It's been a week of great consequence for the media. On Monday, Russell Brand was sentenced to over ten years in prison for rape and sexual assault. Our panel discusses the issues raised: Rosamund Urwin, chief news correspondent at The Sunday Times; Alex Wilson, partner at RPC, and Sarah Ditum, author of Toxic: Women, Fame and The Noughties.

programme.title: Global Eye
programme.desc: A weekly programme from the BBC World Service, bringing forensic journalism from all corners of the world by BBC Eye, the World Service's critically acclaimed investigative unit, and featuring expert global correspondents getting to the heart of the biggest international stories. In this episode: Akisa Wandera reports from Angola, where billions of dollars are being poured into a vast new trade corridor at the centre of a global race for critical minerals. We examine what's at stake for the people living on the frontline of this transformation. Plus: BBC Brasil travels to the city of Camaçari, where Chinese carmaker BYD has opened its biggest factory in Latin America. As Chinese investment reshapes jobs, industry and daily life, we explore how one Brazilian city has become a test case for the growing rivalry between China and the United States.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: Two drivers stage a crash and pursue a £60,000 insurance payout. But they overlook one crucial detail: the dashcam records their scheming as well as the smash. In Liverpool, Gail Caldwell faces two cars heading the wrong way down a motorway slip road, while another driver runs a red light with a pedestrian on the crossing. Dashcams capture all the evidence investigators need to get justice.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Programme in which experts uncover the various tricks of the property auction trade

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: In this special episode, four well-known Radio DJs go head-to-head at one of Britain’s biggest antiques fairs to raise money for charity. Hoping to spin loads of profits are BBC Radio 2’s OJ Borg and his teammate Melvin Odoom opposite BBC Asian Network’s Nikita Kanda and Radio 1’s Maia Beth. Let’s hope their antiques experts Izzie Balmer and Nick Hall are on the same wavelength as they hunt for bargains among the stalls. A brass pipe sparks a conversation about foreign languages for the reds, but are they speaking the right lingo when it comes to negotiating a good price on some Scandinavian jewellery? Across the fair, Nikita and Maia take a shine to a tatty footstool in the form of a bulldog, but Nick doubts it has any pedigree, and the musical blues compose their own Bargain Hunt song as they try to drum up a profit. At the auction in Chippenham, Izzie confounds her team with a Japanese bonus buy, while Nick hopes his will take off with the bidders.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: The Northumbria Mysteries
programme.desc: When estate agent Luke Wandle is found brutally murdered in his own office, Rose and Raj are met with a tangled web of motives. Naturally, suspicion falls on the two people who discovered the body: Luke’s wife, Catherine, and his business partner Damon. But as the investigation deepens, the suspect list rapidly expands to include an embittered former employee with an axe to grind, and Luke’s tight-lipped secretary and her controlling husband, all hiding secrets of their own.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A couple from the Surrey town of Epsom enjoy the spectacular landscape in Argyll and Bute as Nicki Chapman provides them with some expert property advice. For their budget of £600,000, they want a house with views that just keep on giving. Nicki also takes to the water on Loch Lomond to meet a family who have owned and lived on an island for 70 years.

programme.title: The Bidding Room
programme.desc: Looking to mix things up is Sarah, bearing an impressive silver-plated lighthouse-shaped cocktail shaker. She’s brought her own Elvis impersonator to woo the dealers, but she might get even more help from our very own Nigel Havers. Jason continues to bring the bling, with a uranium glass jewellery set that radiates class. He clearly has a great eye, but will the dealers share his taste? Third to face the dealers is Kamran from Bradford. He’s got a papal artefact he found in the attic, and backed up by some diligent research, he’s looking to move it on. Clayton doesn’t know much about his jade disc, but that just means it might be a sleeper hit. So, will he be able to earn a pretty penny on this charity shop find? Smoking may be bad for your health, but selling smoking memorabilia can be good for your bank balance. Danni’s stylish cigar cutters certainly fit the bill, but the buyers will have to work hard, as she won’t let them go for a snip.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, where in this edition, a team of pop stars featuring Sinitta, Ian 'H' Watkins from Steps, Ritchie Neville from Five and Una Healy from The Saturdays get together to take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash for their chosen charities.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: BBC Children in Need brings the nation together for a spectacular evening of entertainment, warmth and sparkle, with more than a sprinkle of Hollywood stardust. Live from MediaCityUK in Salford, hosts Mel Giedroyc, Sara Cox, Alex Jones, Rylan and Tyler West lead a star-studded show packed with famous faces, dazzling performances, exclusive sketches and big surprises. Highlights on the night include special collaborations with much-loved BBC shows, plus the heartwarming return of the Children in Need Choir, who sing a special medley live. The One Show Challenge Squad take centre stage again as new recruits Zoe and Serena tackle epic challenges to help make a difference to other young lives. Radio 2's Owain Wyn Evans is live in the studio for a hero's welcome after completing his gruelling 400-mile four nations cycle challenge in aid of this year’s appeal. Alongside the glitz and glamour, inspiring stories from children and young people across the UK highlight the life-changing impact of BBC Children in Need.

Chi turns to her list of ‘things you should have done’ in this time of need and opts to do ‘get therapy’, something her parents always knew she’d need to do anyway. This sees her path collide with Ruth, a totally unhinged, tough-love grief counsellor, whose questionable methods leave a lot to be desired. Ruth manhandles Chi’s list and vows to help her get over her grief and move on from being able to see her dead parents.

Out of answers, the family seek advice from grief counsellor Ruth, who advises them to think outside the box and be entrepreneurial. Chi’s not entirely sure what this means, but she needs money. Dave reveals he has a very rich estranged sister, Claudia, whom he hasn’t spoken to since Brexit. It’s risky reaching out to her - she’s a bit of a snob - but if he plays his cards right, he thinks she may well clear his debts.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Grief counsellor Ruth has had enough of Chi feeling down in the dumps due to multiple bereavements in a short space of time, even though it’s a perfectly natural way to feel, and Ruth is literally paid to listen. Ruth sets Chi the task of comparing herself to those less fortunate and instructs her to help out at a food bank - something Ruth does to make herself feel better. Meanwhile, Dave and Lucas are feeling the financial squeeze and settling for a dinner of bread and cress, with only ten pounds left to their name. Chi informs them that she is giving back by going to the food bank and asks if they want to come along.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi is rightfully asked if she’s ‘thick’ for bothering an electrician working on an out-of-order lift. For once in her life, Chi is forced to reconcile with her own intelligence. At her weekly grief counselling sessions, Ruth doesn’t exactly hold back, telling Chi she is indeed simple and not to bother seeking adult education. Chi sets out to prove her wrong and breaks into Ramsgate College in search of an education.

programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: Chi’s ghost parents tell her she should really be worried about dying alone and encourage her to find a life partner. Meanwhile, Lucas gets a job at the cinema but is crumbling under the pressure and the perfectly normal expectations of his manager, Kenneth. programme.title: Things You Should Have Done
programme.desc: It’s Chi’s last free therapy session, and Ruth wants to know whether Chi can still see her dead parents or whether she’s learned anything at all from the counselling. But she very much can still see her dead parents; in fact, they were just in the hallway, wearing outdoor clothes and discussing what will become of them if they leave the house. Will they pass on to another plane? Will this be the end of them?

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: With the promise of unimaginable computing power, a global race for quantum supremacy is raging. Hannah Fry looks inside the IBM research facility, one of the oldest tech companies in the world, to uncover the future of quantum technology. She explores the unprecedented potential of quantum computing and how precarious this advanced power may be in the wrong hands. Through her exclusive interviews with world-class experts in quantum technologies, Hannah explores the international quantum arms race between the US and China. She breaks down the implications of this 21st-century race and how a quantum future could change the very nature of humanity.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity’s future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation.

programme.title: John Simpson - 60 Years at the BBC
programme.desc: John Simpson looks back at his extraordinary 60-year career at the BBC - reporting on the biggest global stories of the era. In a frank, personal and revealing documentary, he reflects on the changing world he has witnessed: the revolution in Iran that seemed destined to fail, his brutal kidnapping in Beirut, the fall of the Berlin Wall, two wars in Iraq, the invasion of Afghanistan and a mind-altering trip up the Amazon. From the Broadcasting House newsroom in 1966 to World Affairs editor, he looks back at memorable encounters with inspiring leaders and cruel dictators - the figures who have shaped history, including Nelson Mandela, Margaret Thatcher, Saddam Hussein, Colonel Gaddafi and Volodymyr Zelensky. The programme also features his insights into the role of the BBC today and the challenges faced in the age of fake news.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Bioacoustics technology and AI have allowed scientists to not only decode complex animal sound data but also begin communicating with animals. In her quest to learn about the current state of animal communication, Professor Hannah Fry travels across the world, meeting Cash the talking dog in California and deciphering elephant rumbles in Nairobi. She looks into the question of whether the emerging ability to communicate with animals is one that should be exploited.

programme.title: Angels One Five
programme.desc: Second World War drama relating the Battle of Britain through the eyes of the operations room of a Kent fighter station during the summer of 1940. A young, inexperienced pilot has trouble settling into the routine of squadron life, and his adherence to the rule book puts him out of favour with his comrades. Can he win them round?

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team enter Border country as the Roadshow visits Manderston, near Berwick-upon-Tweed. Amongst the items featured are pieces from Queen Victoria's household, a gruesome man trap and Lord Palmer's collection of rare biscuit tins.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from Rochester Cathedral in Kent. Antiques expert Elizabeth Talbot falls for a book of fairy tales illustrated by Arthur Rackham, and Adam Partridge discovers an elegant chiming Swiss pocket watch. Presenter Paul Martin meets one of the last remaining survivors of the Dunkirk evacuation during the Second World War.

programme.title: House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Dame Laura Kenny, Minah Shannon, Seann Walsh and Ricky Wilson take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted with the House of Games record player?

programme.title: Strictly - It Takes Two
programme.desc: Ellie Taylor is on hand with more Strictly exclusives as she’s joined by a brand new all-star panel to break down the couple’s next dances.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage from Hampden as Scotland host North Macedonia in the Nations League.

programme.title: Die Hard with a Vengeance
programme.desc: Classic action blockbuster. John McClane (Bruce Willis) and a store owner, Zeus (Samuel L Jackson), must play a bomber's deadly game as they race around New York trying to stop him.

programme.title: Blue Story
programme.desc: A feature adaptation of Rapman's YouTube series about two young south London friends from different boroughs and their deepening relationships with gangs and girls.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: Desperate to recover their losses, the Phelans strike a deal with Ozzie Thompson. At Jamie and Melissa’s engagement party, Michael and Diana attempt to broker peace with the family. Meanwhile, Freddie spirals further out of Michael’s control.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: Hollywood legend Bill Murray begins a journey around Ireland, combining golf with a search for his Irish roots. But travelling with Bill rarely goes to plan. In Kinsale, chance encounters turn a simple walk into an adventure, while friend and golf writer Tom Coyne tries to keep things on track. Golf brought Bill to Ireland, but the best moments often happen far from the course.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Whether you were wading through floods or struggling through a heatwave, 2026 was the year when you could hardly miss our extreme weather. Temperatures in the summer topped 30C for 33 days in a row. Months earlier, some parts of the UK saw 40 consecutive days of rain. The BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt investigates the impact of climate change on our weather. He speaks to scientists who warn that hotter summers and wetter winters are likely to become more typical, and asks if enough is being done to adapt our towns and cities to the changing climate. As the cost of living continues to bite, are governments under pressure to ditch some green policies or do they remain committed to tackling climate change?

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Brinicle invites Pancake onto his radio show but is cross when his accidental burps prove a hit. Pancake soon discovers that fame as ‘burping guy’ has its downsides.

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Dad and Cosima both think they're the best at pranking. Their prank war quickly spirals out of control, until Big Lizard finally reveals Proxima's real pranking champion!

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: It's bathtime! The ducklings are determined Weasy will get clean.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: The Gnome Crystal Mine has ground to a halt, leaving the forest with no crystals, no power supply and melting ice lollies! The heroes are tasked with a quest to find out what has happened and to fix it. It turns out that a slimy beast named Smarg has made the mine her home. But with Hoofius’s fear of gunk getting the better of him, evicting the slippery Smarg is not going to be easy.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings use magic Chinese lanterns for sound and light shows.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is a referee at a football match, and Frog sees how much a footballer is cheered for scoring a goal. He is desperate to score one himself, but can he get past Duck's red card?

programme.title: Pokémon Horizons
programme.desc: Liko worries that Hattrem could be holding itself back for the sake of others.

programme.title: Winx Club - The Magic Is Back
programme.desc: The dark magic of Vexius has contaminated Alfea with a lethal residue. The Winx, together with Flora's parents, are searching for a cure to save the flora and fauna of the magic kingdom.

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Newsround
programme.desc: Topical news magazine for children.

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini and Abby go head-to-head in an epic Children in Need racing challenge, and Tyler West and Hacker make some delicious Pudsey Pizzas.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve seeks out deadly creatures in miniature, including Australia’s most beautiful spider, Oman’s deadly deathstalker scorpion and a bright blue beauty in Indonesia.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens, this time in south east Asia. Since the 19th century, western gardeners have loved tropical gardens. Monty visits the archetype - the mysterious Jim Thompson's Garden in Bangkok. He seeks something more authentic in the Royal Palace gardens and the floating gardens of the canals of Bangkok. In Bali, his preconceptions are challenged again. Is the western picture of the exotic garden a construct?

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin explore why geese fly in a V formation, why leaves change colour in autumn and why birds eat rocks.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: In a rare in-depth interview, Sir Rod Stewart and Penny Lancaster welcome Anita Rani into their home to discuss their lives, family, fame and faith, and how Christmases past and present have shaped them. Across an intimate fireside chat, Christmas crafting in a festive greenhouse and a stroll around the stunning grounds of their countryside home, they reflect on Rod’s rise to fame, Penny’s journey from model to special constable and festive traditions, including exchanging gifts with Elton John.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off some sensational breakfasts to kickstart your weekend, including granola and yoghurt cupcakes, a banana and peanut butter bake, and a crazy-but-delicious breakfast pizza.

programme.title: Ice Cold in Alex
programme.desc: During the German offensive in Libya in 1942, Captain Anson, commander of a motor ambulance convoy, finds himself cut off from his unit with only an old ambulance to take him back to Alexandria. His companions are two young nurses and his sergeant, Tom Pugh. As the little party sets off on the long journey, they meet Van der Poel, a South African captain who begs a lift.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin wants to run for the hills because of a tricky legal issue in Devon. Jacqui is in Eastbourne, where work is already under way at an end-of-terrace. And Dion goes to Northampton, where a smelly cellar is hard to cope with!

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin and his team of experts invite members of the public to bring their antiques to be viewed and valued, with an option to sell at auction.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Live coverage as Wales take on Norway in Oslo for their penultimate game in the Nations League.

programme.title: UEFA Nations League
programme.desc: Stephen Watson presents full match coverage from Windsor Park as Northern Ireland take on Ukraine in the Nations League. With just two matches remaining, Northern Ireland remain firmly in contention for promotion from League B. However, Ukraine could provide a major test as Michael O’Neill’s side look to bolster their position ahead of a potentially decisive final fixture. Commentary is by Thomas Kane and Stephen Craigan, with expert analysis from Stuart Dallas, Caragh Hamilton and David Healy.

programme.title: 40 Hits of 1975 at the BBC
programme.desc: Take a musical trip back in time with 40 essential hits from the year 1975, plucked from the BBC’s archives. The punk explosion was two years away, and disco was only just starting to surface, but these 12 months were still packed with classic songs that remain staples to this day. Key moments include ABBA in Blackpool on Seaside Special, the Bay City Rollers riding the wave of Rollermania, and debut hits from key artists who were pioneers in their individual genres, including Bob Marley, Supertramp and Kraftwerk.

programme.title: Godland
programme.desc: In the late 19th century, a young Danish priest is sent to Iceland with a mission to set up a parish in a remote part of the country. Faced with an ambivalent reception by less-than-welcoming locals, he finds that his zeal, faith and sense of reality start to drift as he ventures deeper into the Icelandic landscape. In Danish and Icelandic with English subtitles.

programme.title: This City Is Ours
programme.desc: The tragic events of the party send shock waves through the Phelans. As dangerous secrets threaten to come to light, Michael is forced to make a difficult confession to Diana. Meanwhile, unseen dangers close in, and it becomes clear no-one is safe.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The second leg of the race takes the teams across the heart of Borneo to a modern metropolis on its eastern coast and their second checkpoint.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Anita Rani meets Paralympian and broadcaster Ade Adepitan to hear his inspirational life story and how sport, spirituality and the festive season have shaped him, from contracting polio as a toddler in Nigeria, to growing up with a disability in east London in the 1970s, to the rocky road that led to Paralympic glory with the British wheelchair basketball team. Now a respected broadcaster, Ade shines a light on the causes that are close to his heart.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Figures for the first seven months of the year show milk production in Northern Ireland is heading for a record year. But fluctuating prices, rising costs and the ever-present threat of disease have left many dairy businesses under financial pressure. Alongside local farmer Emily McGowan, Charlotte Smith and Adam Henson explore how dairy farmers across County Antrim, one of Northern Ireland's most productive dairy regions, are turning to tech and innovative business models to build a more resilient future. Adam also introduces this year’s BBC Food and Farming Awards Countryfile Young Countryside Champion nominees.

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: Dougie is in Castlemilk housing estate on the southern edge of Glasgow, where he explores a local nature reserve that has transformed from perceived no-go zone to a thriving, green place. Arlene steps back in time in Aberdeenshire as she visits a rare shoemaker's workshop that shut up shop over 80 years ago. She meets the locals carefully conserving the shop’s contents. Anne is in the Black Isle, finding out about a charity funded by Children in Need that is providing bereavement support across the Highlands. And Dougie watches on as one couple’s herd of Aberdeen Angus cattle leaves the farm for good to go under the hammer at a dispersal sale.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: Radio 1 presenter Sian Eleri follows Pudsey Bear’s clues on a road trip around Wales to meet the special young people and projects benefiting from BBC Children in Need funding.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen Best Bites
programme.desc: Andi Oliver takes a classic British dessert and transforms it into a savoury number with her three cheese and leek bread and butter pudding. She then grills slices of it with a rarebit sauce on top, serving it with a leek and spinach veloute. Niklas Ekstedt brings the taste of Sweden to the studio with the iconic Jansson's temptation, which he serves alongside a deliciously fatty pork chop. Sabrina Ghayour serves up three tasty treats that are perfect for sharing: lamb barberry and pine nut koftas, pomegranate-glazed aubergines, and muhammara dip. Rick Stein has a dish inspired by his travels, while Paul A Young makes maraschino cherry and almond truffles. And Mel C is in the hot seat to face either her food heaven, roast lamb, or her food hell, okra. Meanwhile, Rick Stein has a peek behind the scenes at how the filming of his shows doesn’t always go to plan, and Clive Myrie gets a taste of Caribbean honey.

programme.title: Best Bakes Ever
programme.desc: With Britain more obsessed with baking than ever, actress and cake expert Jane Asher brings together a selection of recipes from the nation's favourite television chefs, for 'The Best Bakes Ever'. Each episode gives baking fans another chance to experience classic dishes from the likes of the James Martin, Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, the Hairy Bikers, Raymond Blanc, Nigella Lawson, Tom Kerridge, Lorraine Pascale and Rachel Khoo. There's added insight and appreciation from Jane herself too. Whether its cakes, pies, puddings or main courses - this greatest hits of baking is a must for anyone with a need to knead, and should help inspire even more of us to start getting creative in the kitchen.

programme.title: Nigel Slater's Simple Suppers
programme.desc: Nigel Slater creates simple but delicious meals from ingredients that are often overlooked, including a lentil and chard stew.

programme.title: Jane Eyre
programme.desc: Charlotte Bronte's classic about an orphan girl who grows up to become a governess in a gloomy manor in Yorkshire, where she falls in love with the mysterious Edward Rochester.

programme.title: Spellbound
programme.desc: Gripping Hitchcock thriller in which a psychoanalyst falls in love with her new boss, knowing that he is an amnesiac who may be a killer and an impostor. Characteristically Hitchcockian twists blur reality and imagination as the psychoanalyst struggles to restore his memory. A dream sequence designed by Salvador Dali adds to the suspense.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This episode contains a collection of interesting and previously unseen finds from the show's travels round the country, visiting Margam Country Park in south Wales, Highcliffe Castle in Dorset and Powderham Castle in Devon. The experts include Catherine Southon, Adam Partridge, Philip Serrell, Will Axon, Christina Trevanion and Mark Stacey, with items ranging from a South African Krugerrand coin to a rare walnut-shaped Japanese flintlock. Paul also takes a look at the treasures and lavish interiors at Firle Place in east Sussex.

programme.title: Golf: Tour Championship
programme.desc: Final day highlights as the DP World Tour season reaches its climax. The winner of the Race to Dubai is crowned, with Northern Ireland’s Rory McIlroy having won the last four editions. McIlroy has won seven Race to Dubai titles, putting him one behind Colin Montgomerie’s all-time record. Spain’s Engenio Chacarra has enjoyed an incredible breakout season, and the USA’s Patrick Reed is firmly in the mix with two wins to his name. Open champion Ryan Fox and PGA champion Aaron Rai also tee it up on the Earth Course at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai. The top ten DP World Tour members not already exempt will earn a PGA Tour card for the 2027 season.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The third leg of the race sees the teams leave behind the ancient jungles of Borneo to reach the island of Sulawesi, an Indonesian wonderland that lies far from the tourist trail. But with the end of Ramadan fast approaching, the teams must negotiate the crowds heading home for Eid al-Fitr.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: As the days grow longer, the MacDonalds round up their pregnant Highland cattle on the tiny island of Vallay off North Uist for a prenatal check up and vitamin boost. In Newtonmore in the Cairngorms, Jenni’s new alpaca arena is finally finished, which means her menagerie of alpacas, donkeys and goats must be moved to their new home. Nikki and Ollie are speculating to accumulate in Moray, splashing out on a new honesty shack.

programme.title: Eva Longoria: Searching for France
programme.desc: Paris is home to more award-winning pastry chefs than anywhere else in the world. Here, the day revolves around patisserie. Morning begins with the buttery flakes of a croissant. At midday, a baguette tucked under the arm signals lunch. And by the afternoon, mouthwatering sweet treats are savoured like miniature works of art. Resistance is futile, and Eva is seduced by the Paris-Brest, a rum baba, the macaron, a mango cake and dahlia, to name just a few.

programme.title: Ireland with Simon Reeve
programme.desc: Simon begins his journey in the south of Ireland, paramotoring with an Irish explorer. On the west coast, he does a spot of surfing before climbing Croagh Patrick in honour of Ireland's patron saint. This leg of his journey ends in Malin Head, Ireland's most northerly point.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Bob and Paul are in County Durham, fishing the River Tees for a rare species of wild brown trout. They navigate the area through the lens of a six-year-old Bob as he takes Paul on a trip along the landscapes of his youth. Bob lost his dad when he was very young, but some of the memories he holds dear to him are of the fishing trips they used to go on. Later, Bob invites their old friend Reece Shearsmith to dinner, who has some particularly spooky local tales to tell them about the River Tees.

programme.title: A Course Called Ireland
programme.desc: As Bill's 75th birthday approaches, brother Joel joins the adventure, bringing some Murray family rivalry to the golf course. Comedian Joanne McNally attempts her first ever round, while a bouncing boat trip to the Cliffs of Moher brings further unexpected encounters. Then friends and familiar faces gather to celebrate a milestone birthday – and a reflective Bill looks ahead to what might come next.

programme.title: Later... with Jools Holland
programme.desc: Jools Holland introduces a special edition of the show starring one of the biggest bands in the world, Fontaines D.C. Marking the release of their album Dopamine Chamber, the Dublin five-piece take to the stage for an intimate performance filmed at Alexandra Palace Theatre in north London. Ahead of a huge global arena and stadium tour, including two nights at the iconic Slane Castle in Ireland, the band play exclusive first performances of tracks alongside unique versions of favourites from their extensive songbook.

programme.title: The Hurt Locker
programme.desc: Baghdad, 2004. A maverick member of a US military unit tackling IEDs and bomb disposal aggravates his teammates. Powerful Oscar- and BAFTA-winning drama.

programme.title: This is CBBC!

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Shaun is in serious trouble when the Farmer discovers he is the cake thief who has sabotaged his baked goods. When another farmer arrives and begins negotiations with the Farmer, Shaun fears the worst. Is this the end of our hero's time on Mossybottom Farm?

programme.desc: Herbert is starting to feel his age and secretly drinks from the Fountain of Youth. However, his desire to be young puts the whole quest in jeopardy.

When the contest arrives, it is revealed Stevie was only pretending to be Boy's friend to keep him from practicing! But maybe Boy has a trick of his own up his sleeve...

programme.desc: Grizzy gets his hands on a machine that can sculpt ice.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The Lemmings find an ice block that holds a frozen prehistoric animal.

programme.title: SpongeBob SquarePants
programme.desc: Plankton's pet amoeba Spot has puppies.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck becomes a magician’s assistant at a magic show. Everything is going well until Frog decides that the magician’s wand is just what he needs to give him endless riches.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog have a new job washing cars. While Duck carefully cleans each car to a perfect shine, Frog dreams of driving a swanky sports car.

programme.title: Odd Squad

programme.desc: Steve Backshall meets the most ravenous shark in the sea, the tiger shark. Known for eating tin cans and even car number plates, these sharks are in fact perfectly honed hunters.

programme.title: Horrible Histories
programme.desc: Featuring the rather eccentric Georgian philosopher Jeremy Bentham, super-rich Roman politician Crassus, who raps about his blinging lifestyle, and some unusual soldiers who are recruited to fight in WWII. Also, Johannes Gutenberg goes head-to-head with some monks on The Historical Apprentice.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Naturalist Steve Backshall heads to the Bahamas in order to get up close and personal with a whole bunch of sharks. There are plenty of shark species to choose from and Steve has his work cut out deciding which ones are worthy of a place on his Deadly 60 list. Hooking up with shark scientists helps him decide and gives him an opportunity to release some baby sharks into the wild, and he learns how to hypnotise them with his bare hands. Getting mobbed by hungry reef sharks and swimming with a four-metre tiger shark are all in a day's work for Steve and the team!

programme.title: Operation Ouch!
programme.desc: The doctors reveal why your body can't survive without oxygen for more than three minutes, and they find out what it's like to be 999 call handlers in Operation Takeover. Dr Xand investigates how Formula One race car technology can help hospitals, and Dr Chris hits the wards in Ouch and About On Call. Meanwhile in Accident and Emergency, one patient comes in after a bike accident and another has fallen on her wrist.

programme.title: Cooking Buddies
programme.desc: Buddy and Conker are joined by amazing Irish dancer and Kidz Bop British Sign Language interpreter Maisie! She needs Buddy’s help to make something tasty for her dancer friends to top them up after their energetic rehearsals. The only food that can jump as high as Maisie can are pancakes! So, Buddy makes bright green spinach pancakes stacked between layers of ham and an oozy cheese sauce - delicious and sure to knock the socks off her dancer friends! She can have it ready to go before dance class and simply pop it in the oven when she gets home. Maisie teaches Buddy to fingerspell his name in British Sign Language, and he tries to walk in Maisie’s very fast footsteps as he has a go at Irish dancing. Join Buddy, Conker and Maisie as they make a pancake stack that’s flippin’ delicious and will be sure to put a spring in your step, too! You can get all of Buddy’s recipes, and loads more, at bbc.co.uk/food

programme.title: Blow Your Mind
programme.desc: Dr Chris and Dr Xand van Tulleken bring you the top experts on the planet to show you things that will blow your mind. In this episode they find out what cats get up to when we aren't around. We go undercover to follow cats who have amazing GPS systems fitted, and watch what they get up to when we look through specially designed cat cameras.

programme.title: The Dengineers
programme.desc: Vilonu is a huge CBBC fan and dreams of becoming a TV presenter when she is older. She wants a space where she can write, film and edit her very own TV shows.

programme.title: One Zoo Three
programme.desc: It’s vet day at the zoo. Kanu the penguin gets treated for his unhappy feet, Ellie the porcupine has an injection of confidence, and Xizi the amur leopard receives some sad news.

programme.title: Our School
programme.desc: The girls reconnect with family for a revealing new history project, and Teni throws herself into a self-defence class after homesickness hits. Meanwhile, some of the boarders are treated to a surprise visit.

programme.title: The Football Academy
programme.desc: Meet the Tottenham Hotspur academy players. Lia Lewis picks her Three of the Best, and Dominic Solanke takes on 11-year-old Konan in Skill Showdown.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: While exploring a reef, Shellington and Dashi accidentally trigger a feeding frenzy with multiple sharks biting at anything that moves. As Barnacles and Tweak work frantically to plan a rescue, Shellington and Dashi try not to become shark food!

programme.title: Big Lizard
programme.desc: Cosima, Big Lizard and Ammon are squabbling over Dad's precious explorer notebook when disaster strikes. Only by working together can they save it from being lost forever!

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: When Pancake’s precious golden algae go missing, all the Piri friends fall under suspicion. Pancake turns detective and replays the evening - but the solution is far from obvious!

programme.title: Do Not Watch This Show
programme.desc: Wizz's embarrassing parents visit and try to force him to jump over a cactus.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck and Frog are working at a woodland holiday park when they both get lost in the wilderness. Frog heroically leads the way - he's just not sure where to!

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: When the kids won't stop being loud, Mouse uses an invention that causes the others to swap voices so they can hear how irritating they sound. At first the kids have fun with each other’s voices, using them to playing tricks - but how will Boy get through school when all he can say is ‘meow’?

programme.title: The Next Step: Cheer
programme.desc: When a legendary coach abruptly leaves a highly successful cheerleading gym, the team are left in disarray, The Next Step’s Kenzie steps in to take over what’s left of the team, desperate to prove she is more than just a dancer, and that she can build this rag-tag group of athletes into a contender for nationals.

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall and the Deadly crew find themselves in deep water as they head into the flooded forests of Brazil. The water is teeming with life and Steve takes a swim in a piranha-infested river in order to find out more about these killer fish. They are assured of a place on the Deadly 60 list until other mysterious fish lurking in the depths make Steve think again. Determined to see one of the strangest animals that inhabit the waters of the flooded forest, Steve and the team go in search of pink river dolphins, and an encounter with one of the most venomous snakes on the planet rounds off this flooded forest adventure.

programme.title: Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: An all-night gaming session turns the Farmer and Bitzer into sleep-deprived zombies the next day. Shaun takes the chance to change Bitzer’s checklist to suit himself, but he manages to miss the final item: shearing time!

programme.title: Dennis & Gnasher Unleashed!
programme.desc: Dennis and the gang take on the power of WilburCorp to stop Walter’s new line of collectable toys ruining the Beanotown environment with all its wasteful plastic packaging.

programme.title: Danger Mouse
programme.desc: In order to stop a deranged Victorian time-travelling chimp from uninventing the world, Danger Mouse and Penfold must arrive in the past just before the nick of time.

programme.title: Super Happy Magic Forest
programme.desc: Forest inspectors pay the forest a visit to check its super-happy status. Friendlyface sends the heroes on outlandish quests to guarantee results.

programme.title: Boy Girl Dog Cat Mouse Cheese
programme.desc: When Cat coughs up a magic hairball, the siblings use it to make all their decisions for them. However, when the hairball leads them to give away all their possessions, they realise it might not be so magical after all.

programme.title: Grizzy and the Lemmings
programme.desc: The extraordinary animals from a tablet game come to life after the device explodes.

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: When Duck is selling ice cream on the beach from his ice cream van, Frog really wants to find the prize-winning golden lolly stick and will go to any lengths to get it!

programme.title: Duck and Frog
programme.desc: Duck is working on the check-in desk at an airport and won't allow Frog to check in his enormous suitcase. Will Frog be able to slim it down and catch his plane?

programme.title: Pablo: Next Level
programme.desc: Pablo loves art and is excited by the idea of making a clay pot. But when Mouse sees the clay, she gets freaked out by the texture and doesn’t want Pablo to touch it.

programme.title: Monster Loving Maniacs
programme.desc: Bo and Ernest visit Wolf Bro inside the Soul Connection. But they are not alone.

programme.title: That's Jokes
programme.desc: Hilariously silly animated sketch comedy. Follow the drama of the talking guinea pigs of Hutch Street, or watch as Guy Reader tries to get through a news report without something going horribly wrong. Experience the real thoughts of your bins, and then get a lesson in manners from Posh Pom. Watch as documentary animals break character, find out where Billy burps, and see the trendiest grannies and grandads ever!

programme.title: Blue Peter
programme.desc: Shini and Abby go head-to-head in an epic Children in Need racing challenge, and Tyler West and Hacker make some delicious Pudsey Pizzas.

programme.title: Pudsey and the Thread of Hope
programme.desc: Uplifting 25-minute animated special inspired by Children in Need. Nine-year-old Jai is struggling with the loss of his dad.
